Commentary.Commentary: Right then! It was our pleasure to bring this magnificent game of cricket to you and we hope that you all enjoyed it. That is all we have from this game, but these two teams will fight again in the third and final ODI. It will be played on 16th July at 1045 Local (0945 GMT). Do join us for that. Till then, take care and goodbye!

Andy Balbirnie, Ireland skipper, is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH, he says that he is extremely proud of the way they played. Adds that they showed character and bowled and batted really well. Says that Tector's innings was brilliant and he is really developing into a strong player. Further adds that they will have a couple of beers to celebrate the win. Adds that McBrine's innings was very important. About his batting, says that it was exciting to face the Proteas bowlers.

Temba Bavuma, South Africa skipper, says that Ireland outplayed us. Says that there is a lot of things to work on. Says that the plan was to get wickets in the first Powerplay. Adds that 100 runs in the last 10 overs, put them under pressure. Says that there were not many partnerships as well apart from the one between Janneman Malan and Rassie van der Dussen and that put a lot of pressure on the middle order.

Earlier in the day, Ireland scored 290 as Andy Balbirnie scored a ton and Harry Tector and George Dockrell batted well towards the end. The South African bowlers had a rough day as they were taken apart by the batters. South Africa had a tough day with their fielding also as they spilled catches which they would take 9 out of 10 times. Their spinners did well but the pacers took a hammering. In the end, the total of 290 ended up more than enough as they won by 43 runs.

Ireland had a good start with the ball as Craig Young and Josh Little took early wickets. There was a solid stand between Malan and van der Dussen in the middle, that threatened to take the game away from them. But George Dockrell and Andy McBrine struck in successive overs to tilt things back in their favour. After that, Little took one and Simi Singh took the wicket of Miller to put them in firm control of the game. Their bowlers did a tidy job in the final overs to finish things off. Mark Adair, McBrine and Little took 2 wickets each. The rest of the bowlers took one and it was a team performance that won them this game! Their fielding was also top-notch and they rarely made any mistakes.

South Africa would have wanted to get a strong start but that did not happen as they lost Aiden Markram and Temba Bavuma quite early. But Janneman Malan and Rassie van der Dussen put on a good stand in the middle overs to keep them in the hunt. Unfortunately for them, Malan fell in the 33rd over for 84 and van der Dussen fell in the very next over for 49. They would have wanted a good partnership after that but Verreynne fell for 13 and the required rate kept climbing. They lost Miller and Phehlukwayo too in quick succession and things kept getting out of their control. In the end, they fell short by 43 runs.

A famous win for Ireland as they have beaten South Africa for the first time and they will remember this for a while! They were the better of the two teams and have deserved this victory. South Africa, on the other hand, had a very tough day at office and will be very disappointed with the way they played.

A full ball, on off. Bavuma works it to mid off.
A length ball, on middle. Bavuma hops and blocks it out.
A length ball, around off, nips back in after landing. Bavuma looks to drive but gets the inner half of the bat towards the leg side.
Goes wide of the crease and bowls a full ball, on middle. Pushed back to the bowler.
On a length, on middle. Defended out.
FOUR BYES! Misses everyone! A length ball, angling way down the leg side. Malan misses his flick, the keeper fails to collect and the ball runs away to the fine leg fence.
Full ball, on off. Pushed to covers.
FOUR! Where was the third slip? A fuller delivery, around off. Malan looks to drive but gets a thick outside edge wide of second slip towards third man fence.
A good length ball, on middle. Malan blocks it out.
Short ball, on middle. Kept out.
Three slips in place for Bavuma.
A back of a length ball, on middle. Bavuma gets a healthy outside edge off his attempted defense towards third man for a single.
Another edgy run! A length ball, on middle. Bavuma looks to drive but gets inner half towards mid-wicket for a quick single. The fielder scored a direct hit at bowler's end but Bavuma was well in.
A good length ball, angling on middle. Malan looks to defend but gets an inside edge towards fine leg for a single.
A full length ball, on middle. Bavuma chips it over square leg. The fielder runs back, dives and keeps it down to three.
Again on the pads, flicked to mid-wicket.
Lovely shot! A full ball, on middle. Bavuma flicks it through mid-wicket. The fielder runs back and chases it down. Two taken and he is off the mark.
Length ball, just around off. Temba Bavuma shoulders arms to it.
Back of a length, outside off. Malan leaves it alone.
FOUR! Edged and four! Full ball, outside off. Malan goes for it but gets the outside edge. The ball runs to the third man fence.
The skipper, Temba Bavuma walks out to bat now.

OUT! TAKEN! Aiden Markram might have dropped catches in this series, but his catch isn't dropped! Craig Young draws first blood! Hits the deck on a length, around off. Markram looks to go down the ground but gets the top edge. Andy McBrine moves to his left at mid off and takes it with ease.
Commentary.Howout: c Andy McBrine b Craig Young

Commentary.Commentary: Good length ball, outside off. Punched towards covers now.
Back of a length, outside off. Markram rises up and turns this towards square leg.
Short of a length, on off. Markram hops up and pushes it back to the bowler.
Back of a length, on off. Malan blocks it back on the deck. 12 from the over.
SIX! Up and over! Malan comes down the track and lifts this all the way over the cover fence. Lovely shot.
A nice inswinger now, on off. Malan is equal to the task and punches it to covers.
A very full one, on off. Blocked out by Malan.
FOUR! On the charge! Malan comes down the track and chips it over the bowler. The ball does not come from the middle of the bat but the fast outfield means that it runs to the fence.
Full and wide outside off. A bit too wide for the umpire's liking, who has to raise his arms.
Fuller ball, outside off. Markram pushes it to the left of mid off. The fielder runs across and keeps it down to one.
Good length ball, lands outside off. The ball shapes away so Malan decides that he will not chase this one.
Right on the money with his length ball. Malan is solid in his defence of this one.
FOUR! Hammered! Back of a length, outside off. Malan hangs in his crease and pulls it handsomely to the square leg fence.
Fuller ball, outside off. Punched to point now by Malan.
Beaten! Malan comes down the track so Young drags his length back a bit. Malan looks to defend but the ball zips past the outside edge.
Bowls a length ball, right on the off pole. Malan blocks it from the crease.
Short of a length, outside off. Markram shuffles across and blocks it out. 9 from the over.
Drags his length back a bit. Left alone by Markram.
FOUR! Punished! Mark Adair searches for swing and bowls it too full and wide. Markram says thank you very much and drives it past covers for a boundary.
Length ball, on off. Markram blocks it out well.
On the pads. Whipped to deep square leg for one.
FOUR! Lovely drive! Full and wide outside off. Malan leans into it and drives it past point for a boundary.
Who will bowl from the other end? It is Mark Adair who will use the other new ball.
Ends the over with a solid defence. A good start from Craig Young. Just 3 from the first over.
Good length ball, on off. Blocked from the crease.
Serves a length ball, wide enough for Markram to leave it.
Length ball, down the leg side. Wide called again.
Fuller ball, on off. Markram blocks it out.
Length ball, down the leg side. Wide called.
Fuller ball, on off. Pushed to covers now for one.
Beaten! Fuller ball, just outside off. Malan looks to play it from the crease but the ball nips away and goes past the bat.
